# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
- Exposure to observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
- Knowledge of logistics, transport or supply-chain domains, or EDI formats (EDIFACT, X12)
- Dutch or French language skills

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 62,000 – 82,000 gross per year depending on experience
- 28 days of holiday, a learning budget of EUR 1,500 per year and a home-office allowance
- Pension scheme, public-transport card and a modern hybrid office near Antwerpen-Centraal
- A team that values pragmatic engineering, clear documentation and sustainable pace

## How to apply

Send us your CV and, if you like, a short cover letter or links to code you are proud of. We read every application and reply within two weeks. Our interviews are: a 30-minute intro call, a practical technical conversation about a past project and a short system-design discussion.

Tessel Cargo Software is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

Tessel Cargo Software develops software for European freight forwarders, helping them plan routes and loads, book carriers, track shipments and manage digital delivery notes and customs paperwork. Founded in Antwerp in 2017 by former operations managers, it serves more than 340 freight forwarders across 19 countries.

Its values are **“Be dependable. Say what you see. Leave it better.”** Tessel works in small product teams and encourages engineers to own and operate the services they build, including on-call responsibilities. Teams favour short design notes over lengthy specifications and dedicate one day per sprint to reliability. The company also publishes an engineering blog and sponsors a local Python meetup.

Tessel has around 120 employees across Antwerp, Poznań and a remote-first engineering group. Its technology includes Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka and AWS. Following a €24 million Series B round in 2026, it plans to expand its engineering team and develop predictive shipment ETAs.

# Tessel Cargo Software in the news

## Tessel Cargo Software raises EUR 24 million to expand live tracking across Europe
**Antwerp, 12 March 2026**

Tessel Cargo Software, the Antwerp-based provider of routing and tracking software for freight forwarders, announced a EUR 24 million Series B round. The funding will be used to double the engineering team by the end of 2027, extend the Tessel Track API with predictive ETAs and open a second engineering hub in Poznań.

"Forwarders still lose hours every day to chasing status updates," said co-founder and CEO Margot Vandenberg. "Our goal is that a dispatcher never has to phone a driver to ask where a trailer is."

CTO Piotr Lis said the company is migrating its event pipeline from queue-based workers to Kafka streams to support peak loads during the autumn peak season, and is investing in observability and on-call tooling. "We want engineers who enjoy running the things they build," he added.

Tessel says it processed 38 million shipment events per day in February 2026, up 2.4x from a year earlier, and that its tracking API maintained 99.95% availability over the last twelve months.
# Careers at Tessel Cargo Software
*(fictional careers page – tesselcargo.example/careers)*

## Build the software behind Europe's supply chains

**Engineering at Tessel**
- Stack: Python (FastAPI), Go for a few high-throughput workers, PostgreSQL, Kafka, AWS (EKS, RDS, S3), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Grafana/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry
- Team structure: product teams of 6-8 engineers with an engineering manager and a product manager
- Practices: trunk-based development, code review within one working day, blameless post-mortems, one week in six on call (with a rota bonus)
- We publish our architectural decisions as short ADRs and invite candidates to read two of them before the interview.

**Benefits:** hybrid work, EUR 1,500 learning budget, 28 days holiday, pension scheme, home-office allowance, company-paid language lessons.

**Hiring process:** intro call (30 min) -> technical conversation about a past project (60 min) -> system-design discussion (60 min) -> meeting with the team and engineering manager. No take-home tests.

**What we look for:** people who have run software in production, communicate clearly in writing, and like understanding the business problem behind a ticket. Logistics experience is a bonus, not a requirement.

**Open roles:** Backend Engineer (Python) – Routing & Tracking · Senior Data Engineer · Site Reliability Engineer · Product Designer · Customer Success Manager (Nordics)
